review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–90) from the supplied source. It has three proofs. (1) `isClosed_singleton_kernelPoint` shows a kernel point is closed by using maximality of the kernel of a surjective map. (2) `exists_kernelPoint_eq_of_isClosed` uses Zariski's lemma, the algebraic-closure bijection, and a kernel computation. (3) `range_kernelPoint_eq_closedPoints` is a thin wrapper that combines the first two. No nontrivial reasoning is repeated across two or more proofs. The only overlap is that the first two proofs both rewrite with `kernelPoint_asIdeal`, which is routine unfolding. A shared lemma there would not meet the rubric. I did not look for duplication against other files, because the rubric concerns repeated machinery within proofs. I did not run Lean, so nothing here was compiled.
